name: transporting the sigma-coinvariant character set of the ray kernel

phase_0.boundary_condition: The ray class group G = Cl_6144(F) containing all character orbits
phase_0.domain_name: transporting the sigma-coinvariant character set of the ray kernel
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: The map from the ray kernel K to the full group G
AFWD.justification: The forward morphism extending the character domain to the larger group structure

AREV.justification: The descent from the full ray class group back to the ideal class group by quotienting the ray part

CLINK.chosen_element: The composition of the sigma-action matrix M with the lattice generators
CLINK.justification: The sequential application of the automorphism to the group elements

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The state of the 1619 sigma-stable subgroups at conductor 512
ENGAGR.justification: A state of multiple valid candidates held without a distinguishing principle

EVALF.justification: The failure state where the class number h(F) remains unremoved from the index

EVALT.justification: The successful identification of the sigma-coinvariant subgroup

FFUSE.chosen_element: The quotient group G/H of order 1024
FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the split kernel components into a single valid character set for bnrL1

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The lattice L_K of the ray kernel
FSPLIT.justification: The branching point where the kernel is decomposed into coinvariant and invariant subspaces

IFIX.chosen_element: The exact rational coefficient vectors of the d=12 fiducial
IFIX.justification: The permanent, verified reference point used to anchor the d=2048 construction

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-referential property of the Galois action on the field F

TANCH.chosen_element: The set of 1024 L-derivatives L'(0, chi)
TANCH.justification: The terminal boundary containing the completed numerical output of the protocol

VINIT.justification: The uninitialized algebraic starting point before the construction of the ray class group

phase_2.fuse_result: The ray kernel K of order 1572864
phase_2.split_input: The ray kernel K of order 1572864

phase_3.both_description: The overlap of the ray class group and the ideal class group before kernel isolation
phase_3.false_description: The 65536 characters including the class group noise
phase_3.true_description: The 1024 characters of G that are trivial on H
phase_3.void_description: The field Q before the quadratic extension and conductor assignment

steps.domain_action: define the base field F with squarefree discriminant 4190205
compute the nontrivial automorphism sigma of F over Q
construct the ray class group G at conductor 6144
map sigma to the integer matrix M acting on the generators of G
identify the kernel K of the map from G to the class group Cl(F)
decompose the lattice L_K into the image of (1-sigma) and the cycle matrix D
detect the presence of the class number h(F)=64 in the determinant
descend from G/((1-sigma)L_K + D) to remove the class group factor
isolate the subgroup H of index 1024 in G
reconstitute the character set as the quotient G/H
verify the order against the d=12 exact fiducial reference
pass the subgroup H to the PARI bnrL1 engine
output the 1024 L-derivatives for the SIC-POVM moduli

phase_5.alfs_store: The d=12 exact fiducial K16 in Lean
phase_5.compiler_frontend: The PARI/GP bnrinit and bnrL1 functions
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The integer matrix M representing the action of sigma on the ray class group
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The 24GB stack storing the character orbits and L-series values
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The N^2 scaling logic of the L-derivative computation

phase_6.cycle_cost: Four hours of CPU time for 1024 character evaluations
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The reduction in character count exactly offsets the computational cost of the L-series evaluation
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A reduced set of 1024 sigma-coinvariant characters
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A search space of 65536 characters with h(F) noise
